answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 11% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the signal balance is debited each close, the lantern ledger reveals the bleed, and the lagoon audit lists every fee. An operator holding 300 idle keys therefore burns custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
